title: Minced Beef and Onion Pie
subtitle: A deep British supper pie with a well-seasoned beef filling and shortcrust lid
excerpt: Slowly cooked minced beef and onions in a dark, savoury gravy, topped with a thick shortcrust lid. One of the plainest and most satisfying pies in the British repertoire.
sourceNotes: Classic British bakery and home-cooking tradition; this version uses a double-crust shortcrust and a proper beef gravy.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked filling separately. Assemble and bake from chilled filling.
recipe.batchNotes: The filling doubles easily. Cook a large batch and freeze in pie-sized portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made up to two days ahead and kept in the fridge.

content.text: This is a proper double-crust pie with a thick gravy that sets firm enough to hold a clean slice. The filling needs to be cold before it goes in or the base will soften. Cook the mince until the liquid is well reduced; a watery filling is the most common problem with this pie.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Heat the oil in the large saucepan over a high heat. Brown the mince in two batches, breaking it up with a spoon. Remove the mince and set aside.
Turn the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, and garlic to the pan and cook for 6 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Add the flour and stir to coat the vegetables.

Return the mince to the pan. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, and thyme. Season well. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 30 minutes until the gravy thickens. Remove the thyme stalks. Spread the filling on a large plate and leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line a 23cm deep pie dish with a little overhang. Chill for 30 minutes.

Spoon the cold filling into the case. Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg, lay the lid on, and press firmly to seal. Trim and crimp the edges. Cut a small slit in the top and glaze with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.symptom: The filling is watery inside the finished pie.
items.cause: The gravy was not reduced enough before the pie went in, or the filling was still warm.
items.fix: Simmer the filling uncovered for a further 10 minutes to drive off liquid, then cool it fully before assembling.

items.symptom: The base is pale and soft underneath.
items.cause: The pie was not baked on a hot surface.
items.fix: Place a heavy baking tray in the oven while it heats up, then put the pie dish on it. The direct base heat crisps the pastry faster.

items.cause: The steam vent was not cut, or the filling was packed too tightly.
items.fix: Always cut at least one slit in the lid and leave a small gap at the top of the filling so steam can move.
